text:
ash: FYI — Zephyr is reporting 5xx spikes from their dedicated pool (re-rank path). Customer Slack + CSM looped. SLA at risk if this persists.

maria: @ash can you paste an example request id? I'll pull logs and check pool health.

ash: request id: req_20260318_8f4a. Saw error rate jump ~PRIORITY at 10:12 UTC. Minimal user impact now but trending up.

sam: copying metrics: p99 latency for re-rank jumped from 180ms -> 1.2s on pool-dedicated-3. CPU pinned on a couple workers, OOMs in the logs.

indra: oncall here. Any recent config/rollouts to dedicated pools? I can run a quick kernel/process check.

ash: No recent deploys. Last config change was autoscale tweak 2 days ago by infra. Might be KV cache pressure — re-rank payloads are long context.

maria: I see repeated `failed to allocate kv_cache` entries in pod logs for pool-dedicated-3. Attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-18T10:12:14Z re-rank: ERROR failed to allocate kv_cache size=1.2GB: out of memory
2026-03-18T10:12:15Z re-rank: WARN retrying request, attempt=2
```

sam: Root cause hypothesis: recent dataset from Zephyr increases seq_len and triggers larger KV footprint -> pressure + OOM -> 503s. 

indra: Short-term mitigation options:
- route Zephyr to pool-dedicated-4 (lower utilization) via routing override
- enable per-request kv_cache eviction (config flag)
- restart affected pods (quick but risky)

ash: Customer needs ETA for a harmless workaround. Which is lowest-risk? 

maria: routing override is safest. I can push a temporary routing rule: `route: customer=zephyr -> pool-dedicated-4` for 30m.

sam: +1. If we route, we should also enable monitoring alert for p99 > 800ms to auto-fallback.

indra: I'll do the override if Maria confirms. Also will add an emergency patch to autoscaler to keep spare capacity for re-rank for the next 24h.

oncall-bot: deploy-guard: Canary check failed for pool-dedicated-4 earlier today but was marked transient; manual routing override requires ack from eng-platform-owners.

maria: ack from eng-platform-owners: @sam @indra — please confirm you approve temporary routing despite canary note.

sam: approved. I accept risk; will stand ready to revert.

indra: approved.

ash: thanks. Maria, please push override and ping the customer with ~15-30m ETA. I'll coordinate with CSM.

maria: Pushing now. Command:
```
redwoodctl route override --customer zephyr --pool pool-dedicated-4 --ttl 1800 --reason "urgent OOM mitigation"
```

maria: override active. Pinged CSM. ETA message queued: "We’re diverting traffic to an alternative capacity pool to restore latency; monitoring in place."

sam: I'm adding an alert rule and a fallback policy to route back to hosted pool if p99 > 800ms for 2 consecutive minutes.

indra: Starting autoscaler patch: short-lived change to min_spare=2 on pool-dedicated-3. Will open PR and merge with fast-track if tests pass.

ash: Estimated timeline: routing override done, customer notified (T+10m); autoscaler patch in ~40m; monitoring + fallback in ~15m. Will keep thread updated.

maria: Customer confirms reduced errors after override. Still watching.

sam: alert rule in place and fallback policy bound.

indra: PR opened and running CI: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/8423

ash: thanks everyone. Postmortem owners? Assign to eng-platform (sam) and infra (indra). CSM + cust success to draft comms.

maria: assigning owners in ticket: infra/indra, eng-platform/sam. I'll create a follow-up ticket for capacity recommendations and model quantization suggestions.

ash: closing interim loop — if errors resurge, escalate to pager. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: incident-note: temporary routing override active; owners assigned; next update required in 2h.
